t:
(a) 
Section 1810 is amended—

        (1) 
by inserting after clause (7) of subsection (a) the following new clause:


“(8) 
To refinance in accordance with subsection (e) of this section an existing loan guaranteed, insured, or made under this chapter.”; and



 
        (2) 
by adding at the end the following new subsection:


“(e)

(1) 
For a loan to be guaranteed for the purpose specified in subsection (a)(8) of this section—

“(A) 
the interest rate of the loan must be less than the interest rate of the loan being refinanced;


“(B) 
the loan must be secured by the same dwelling or farm residence as was the loan being refinanced and such dwelling or residence must be owned and occupied by the veteran as such veteran’s home;


“(C) 
the amount of the loan may not exceed an amount equal to the sum of the balance of the loan being refinanced and such closing costs (including any discount permitted pursuant to section 1803(c)(3)(A) of this title) as may be authorized by the Administrator, under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe, to be included in such loan;


“(D) 
the amount of the guaranty of the loan may not exceed the original guaranty amount of the loan being refinanced; and


“(E) 
the term of the loan may not exceed the original term of the loan being refinanced.



“(2) 
A loan to a veteran may be guaranteed by the Veterans’ Administration under this chapter for the purpose specified in clause (8) of subsection (a) of this section without regard to the amount of outstanding guaranty entitlement available for use by such veteran, and the amount of such veteran’s guaranty entitlement shall not be charged as a result of any guaranty provided for such purpose. For purposes of section 1802(b) of this title, such loan shall be deemed to have been obtained with the guaranty entitlement used to obtain the loan being refinanced.


“(3) 
If a veteran is deceased and if such veteran’s surviving spouse was a co-obligor under an existing loan guaranteed, insured, or made under this chapter, such surviving spouse shall, only for the purpose specified in subsection (a)(8) of this section, be deemed to be a veteran eligible for benefits under this chapter.”.




  
    (b) Section 1819(a) is amended—

        (1) 
by adding at the end of paragraph (1) the following new clause:


“(F) 
To refinance in accordance with paragraph (4) of this subsection an existing loan guaranteed, insured, or made under this section.”; and



 
        (2) 
by adding at the end the following new paragraph:


“(4) 

(A) 
For a loan to be guaranteed for the purpose specified in clause (F) of paragraph (1) of this subsection—

“(i) 
the interest rate of the loan must be less than the interest rate of the loan being refinanced;


“(ii) 
the loan must be secured by the same mobile home or mobile-home lot, or mobile home and mobile-home lot, as was the loan being refinanced and such mobile home (or a mobile home on such lot) must be owned and occupied by the veteran as such veteran’s home;


“(iii) 
the amount of the loan may not exceed an amount equal to the sum of the balance of the loan being refinanced and such closing costs (including any discount permitted pursuant to section 1803(c)(3)(A) of this title) as may be authorized by the Administrator, under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe, to be included in such loan;


“(iv) 
the amount of the guaranty of the loan may not exceed the original guaranty amount of the loan being refinanced; and


“(v) 
the term of the loan may not exceed the original term of the loan being refinanced.



“(B) 
A loan to a veteran may be guaranteed by the Veterans’ Administration under this chapter for the purpose specified in clause (F) of paragraph (1) of this subsection without regard to the amount of outstanding guaranty entitlement available for use by such veteran, and the amount of such veteran’s guaranty entitlement shall not be charged as a result of any guaranty provided for such purpose. For purposes of section 1802(b) of this title, such loan shall be deemed to have been obtained with the guaranty entitlement used to obtain the loan being refinanced.


“(C) 
If a veteran is deceased and if such veteran’s surviving spouse was a co-obligor under an existing loan previously guaranteed, insured, or made under this section, such surviving spouse shall, only for the purpose specified in clause (F) of paragraph (1) of this subsection, be deemed to be a veteran eligible for benefits under this chapter.”.




  
    (c) 

        (1) 
Section 1803(c)(3)(A) is amended by striking out “section 1810(a)(5)” and inserting in lieu thereof “clause (5) or (8) of section 1810(a) of this title or section 1819(a)(1)(F) of this title”. 
 
        (2) 
The second sentence of section 1811(b) is amended by inserting “(other than the refinancing of a loan under section 1810(a)(8) or 1819(a)(1)(F))” after “section 1810(a) or 1819 of this title”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a veterans' loan-refinancing benefit provision with no outside-party process, so the answer should be No. However, it directs the Administrator to prescribe regulations governing which closing costs may be included in refinanced loans. Under the definition, requiring or authorizing agency rulemaking counts as participation, because rulemaking brings the public into the federal decision. The rest of the section (loan terms, entitlement rules, surviving spouse eligibility) is not participation on its own.
fable.s: as may be authorized by the Administrator, under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe, to be included in such loan

qwen_block.w: This section establishes the criteria and procedures for veterans to apply for loan refinancing benefits. It details interest rate requirements, property conditions, and guaranty limits. According to the definition, applications for benefits or grants are explicitly excluded from participation. There is no requirement for public comment, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with non-federal entities before a decision is made.
qwen_block.s: To refinance in accordance with subsection (e) of this section an existing loan guaranteed, insured, or made under this chapter.

opus.w: The section requires the Administrator to issue regulations setting which closing costs can be included in refinancing loans. The definition counts required rulemaking as participation. It might seem like a 'No' because the loans are veterans' benefits, and applying for benefits is not participation. But the label rests on the rulemaking mandate, not on any veteran's loan application.
opus.s: such closing costs (including any discount permitted pursuant to section 1803(c)(3)(A) of this title) as may be authorized by the Administrator, under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe, to be included in such loan
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "No," because this section is about guaranteeing refinanced veterans' home loans, and applications for benefits are excluded. That reading misses one clause. The section directs that allowable closing costs be set "under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe." The definition counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation, and Example 6 confirms that a grant of rulemaking authority counts. That rulemaking requirement is what makes this a "Yes."

2. **Answer.**

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the specific conditions under which the Veterans' Administration may guarantee refinanced loans for veterans. While it mentions that the Administrator shall prescribe regulations, it does not require public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside entities in the creation of those regulations. The primary interaction is the provision of a benefit (loan guarantee) to veterans, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the amount of the loan may not exceed an amount equal to the sum of the balance of the loan being refinanced and such closing costs (including any discount permitted pursuant to section 1803(c)(3)(A) of this title) as may be authorized by the Administrator, under regulations which the Administrator shall prescribe, to be included in such loan
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Administrator prescribing regulations implies a rulemaking process that could involve public comment. However, the text itself does not mandate public participation in that rulemaking, nor does it describe any other form of consultation with outside parties. The primary focus is on the eligibility and terms of loan guarantees for veterans.

Resolution: The section details the criteria for refinancing loans guaranteed by the Veterans' Administration. It specifies interest rates, security requirements, and guaranty amounts. It mentions that the Administrator shall prescribe regulations, but it does not require public participation in creating those regulations. The interaction described is between the government and veterans (beneficiaries), which falls under the exclusion for "applications for benefits."
